paras.en: 6.5.5. Coding. Despite the strong coding benchmark performance of the base model, post-training data still provides a significant boost to both code quality and code correctness. This highlights the benefit of high-quality demonstration data and feedback data for coding use cases. Gemini Apps and Gemini API models use a combination of human and synthetic approaches to collect such data. We evaluate our Gemini Apps models’ coding performance on a set of internally curated prompts, distributed across code use cases and languages. Table 18 reports SxS scores, where Gemini (with Pro) significantly improves upon Bard with an older post-training recipe and based on PaLM 2. Gemini Advanced (with Ultra) further improves upon Gemini (with Pro). Side A
paras.zh: 6.5.5. 编码。尽管基础模型在编码基准测试中表现强劲，但后训练数据仍然为代码质量和正确性提供了显著提升。这凸显了高质量演示数据和反馈数据在编码用例中的益处。Gemini Apps 和 Gemini API 模型结合使用人工和合成方法来收集此类数据。我们在内部策划的一组提示词上评估了 Gemini Apps 模型的编码性能，这些提示词涵盖了不同的编码用例和语言。表 18 报告了 SxS 分数，其中 Gemini（Pro 版）显著优于基于 PaLM 2 并使用较旧后训练配方的 Bard。Gemini Advanced（Ultra 版）进一步优于 Gemini（Pro 版）。Side A

paras.en: During the development of Gemini models, we follow a structured approach to responsible deployment to identify, measure, and manage foreseeable downstream societal impacts of our models, in line with previous releases of Google’s AI technology (Kavukcuoglu et al., 2022). Throughout the lifecycle of a project, we follow the structure below. This section provides more detail about our approach and includes key findings where available. We are committed to ongoing transparency and will continue to provide updated information on our approach and testing in upcoming reports.
paras.zh: 在 Gemini 模型的开发过程中，我们遵循结构化的负责任部署方法，以识别、衡量和管理模型可预见的下游社会影响，这与之前发布的 Google AI 技术一致（Kavukcuoglu 等人，2022）。在整个项目生命周期中，我们遵循以下结构。本节将更详细地介绍我们的方法，并包含可获取的关键发现。我们致力于持续透明，并将在后续报告中继续提供关于我们的方法和测试的最新信息。

paras.en: At Google we apply an impact assessment framework throughout the product development lifecycle related to Google’s AI Principles (Google, 2023). This means we assess the risk and impact of AI models we’re building at both a model-level (e.g. for Gemini API Ultra 1.0, as deployed on Cloud
paras.zh: 在 Google，我们根据 Google 的 AI 原则（Google, 2023）在整个产品开发生命周期中应用影响评估框架。这意味着我们在模型层面（例如，针对部署在 Cloud 上的 Gemini API Ultra 1.0）以及将其嵌入更广泛的产品或服务（例如，针对 Gemini Advanced）时，都会评估所构建 AI 模型的风险与影响。

paras.en: Studio or Vertex AI), and once embedded within a broader product or service (e.g. for Gemini Advanced). 7.1.1. Model Assessment We conduct model impact assessments to identify, assess, and document societal benefits and harms associated with the capabilities of Gemini models. Our impact assessments for Gemini API models describe downstream benefits and risks that we identify, spanning across the models’ modalities (text-to-text; image-to-text; and video-to-text). Model impact assessments are conducted by the Google DeepMind Responsible Development and Innovation team, and are reviewed by the Google DeepMind Responsibility and Safety Council. We draw from various sources in producing impact assessments, including a wide range of literature, external expertise, and our in-house ethics and safety research. Gemini models introduce various benefits to people and society. Gemini models’ various modalities, including language, image and video understanding, can help users process information more efficiently, for example through content summarisation. These efficiency benefits can apply to commercial entities, and can assist use cases dependent on text, image or video processing such as video captioning, analytics or product descriptions. Video and image understanding modalities can also be deployed for social good applications downstream, such as enabling descriptions of visual outputs for accessibility purposes. Generative multimodal models may also raise downstream societal risks, with the Gemini models assessments considering a range of risks previously identified within research such as Weidinger et al. (2021) and Shelby et al. (2023). We assessed a range of content risks such as exposure of users to potentially unsafe content, such as sexually explicit, violent or hateful outputs (Weidinger et al., 2021), child safety harms, and representation harms, subsequently designing evaluations across these domains to enable measurement. Beyond content related risks, we analyzed the potential misuse of capabilities for surveillance applications, particularly for mediato-text capabilities, and considered the broader environmental and economic impact of multimodal models. We are continuously conducting research into emerging risks of advanced models, including for dangerous capabilities (e.g. cyber security threats) which form a part of our evaluation approach (Section 7.4). 7.1.2. Product Assessments Beyond the assessment conducted at the model-level, additional risk assessments are conducted on the products by the Google AI Principles team prior to launch (e.g. on the Gemini Advanced product). These risk and impact assessments, alongside both model- and product-level assurance evaluations, are used to guide mitigation and product delivery efforts, and inform deployment decisions. For Gemini Advanced, we conducted extensive deep-dive red teaming via dogfooding and adversarial testing in the areas of safety, accountability, and inclusion to prepare for the initial experimental rollout of Gemini and subsequent updates. Further cross-functional work helps to ensure appropriate mitigations were adopted before Gemini and its new capabilities or offerings, such as Gemini Advanced, launched. Beyond content safety, these product mitigations included the following: • Clear and relevant explanations to set appropriate expectations that describe Gemini as a way to get direct access to Google AI for a wide range of tasks, including complex tasks. Explanations make clear that this AI-powered system is useful for all sorts of tasks — like preparing for a job interview, debugging code for the first time or writing a pithy social media caption.
paras.zh: Studio 或 Vertex AI），以及一旦嵌入更广泛的产品或服务（例如，针对 Gemini Advanced）。7.1.1 模型评估 我们进行模型影响评估，以识别、评估和记录与 Gemini 模型能力相关的社会效益和危害。我们对 Gemini API 模型的影响评估描述了识别的下游收益和风险，涵盖模型的模态（文本到文本；图像到文本；视频到文本）。模型影响评估由 Google DeepMind 负责任开发与创新团队进行，并由 Google DeepMind 责任与安全委员会审查。我们在制作影响评估时借鉴多种来源，包括广泛的文献、外部专家知识以及我们内部的伦理与安全研究。Gemini 模型为人们和社会带来了多种益处。Gemini 模型的多模态能力，包括语言、图像和视频理解，可以帮助用户更有效地处理信息，例如通过内容摘要。这些效率优势可应用于商业实体，并支持依赖文本、图像或视频处理的用例，如视频字幕、分析或产品描述。视频和图像理解模态也可部署用于下游公益性应用，例如为无障碍目的提供视觉输出的描述。生成式多模态模型也可能引发下游社会风险，Gemini 模型的评估考虑了先前研究中识别的一系列风险，如 Weidinger 等人（2021）和 Shelby 等人（2023）所述。我们评估了一系列内容风险，例如用户接触潜在不安全内容的风险，如色情、暴力或仇恨输出（Weidinger 等人，2021）、儿童安全危害和表征危害，随后设计了跨这些领域的评估以实现度量。除了内容相关风险，我们分析了能力滥用于监控应用的潜在风险，特别是媒体到文本能力，并考虑了多模态模型的更广泛环境与经济影响。我们持续研究先进模型的新兴风险，包括危险能力（例如网络安全威胁），这构成了我们评估方法的一部分（第 7.4 节）。7.1.2 产品评估 除了模型层面的评估，Google AI 原则团队在发布前（例如，针对 Gemini Advanced 产品）还会对产品进行额外的风险评估。这些风险与影响评估，连同模型级和产品级的保障评估，用于指导缓解措施与产品交付工作，并为部署决策提供信息。对于 Gemini Advanced，我们通过内部自用和对抗性测试在安全、责任与包容性领域进行了广泛的深度红队测试，以准备 Gemini 的初始实验性发布及后续更新。进一步的跨职能工作确保在 Gemini 及其新能力或产品（如 Gemini Advanced）发布前采用了适当的缓解措施。除了内容安全，这些产品缓解措施包括：• 清晰且相关的解释以设定适当期望，说明 Gemini 是直接访问 Google AI 以完成广泛任务（包括复杂任务）的一种方式。解释表明，这个由 AI 驱动的系统对各种任务都有用——比如准备求职面试、第一次调试代码或撰写精炼的社交媒体标题。

paras.en: • Disclosure in the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice stating that people should not rely on Gemini’s responses as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice. • Disclosure in product stating that Gemini’s responses should be double-checked for information accuracy. • Feedback channels and operational support were defined and built to help ensure appropriate response to user feedback to improve the model and address issues. For the Gemini API Ultra model, that will be available through Google AI Studio and Cloud Vertex AI, product review outcomes resulted in additional safety evaluations on enterprise-specific data across modalities, and additional product-level mitigations to promote safe and responsible use including: • Safety filters with Cloud established thresholds as the default product behavior. • Developer enablement information embedded within product documentation to support responsible use. • Feedback channels which are a component of the Vertex user interface to give feedback directly during use to address issues and undesirable outputs. We are increasingly integrating our AI review work into our holistic enterprise risk management frameworks for assuring the quality of our offerings. This evolution helps us further the scale of our work and integration into existing governance and company-wide infrastructure and accountability processes. In close coordination with central AI Principles review teams, some of our product areas, including Google Cloud, have developed their own specialized review processes, deploying approaches tailored to their unique circumstances.
paras.zh: • 在 Gemini 应用程序隐私声明中进行披露，说明人们不应依赖 Gemini 的回复作为医疗、法律、财务或其他专业建议。• 在产品中披露，说明应再次核对 Gemini 回复的信息准确性。• 定义并构建了反馈渠道和运营支持，以确保对用户反馈作出适当回应，从而改进模型并解决问题。对于将通过 Google AI Studio 和 Cloud Vertex AI 提供的 Gemini API Ultra 模型，产品审查结果导致对跨模态的企业特定数据进行了额外的安全评估，并采取了额外的产品级缓解措施以促进安全负责任的用途，包括：• 以 Cloud 设定的阈值作为默认产品行为的安全过滤器。• 嵌入产品文档中的开发者赋能信息，以支持负责任的用途。• 作为 Vertex 用户界面组件的反馈渠道，以便在使用过程中直接提供反馈以解决问题和不良输出。我们正日益将 AI 审查工作整合到整体企业风险管理框架中，以确保我们产品的质量。这一演进有助于我们扩大工作规模，并融入现有的治理和全公司基础设施及问责流程。在与中央 AI 原则审查团队的密切协调下，包括 Google Cloud 在内的一些产品领域开发了自身的专业化审查流程，部署了针对其独特情况的方法。

paras.en: We have developed a set of model safety policies for Gemini models to steer development and evaluation. The model policy definitions act as a standardized criteria and prioritization schema for responsible development and define the categories against which we measure launch readiness. Google products that use Gemini models, like our conversational AI service Gemini and Cloud Vertex API, further implement our standard product policy framework which is based on Google’s extensive experience with harm mitigation and rigorous research. These policies take product use cases into account – for example, providing additional safety coverage for users under 18. Our model safety policies reflect our established approach towards product safety and preventing harm in consumer and enterprise contexts. Policy areas include generation of child sexual abuse and exploitation content, hate speech, harassment, dangerous content such as guidance on how to make weapons, and malicious content. We also aim to reduce bias in our models via guidelines focused on providing content that reflects our global user base. In addition, we have guidelines that prioritize providing neutral answers grounded in authoritative, consensus facts, or providing multiple perspectives where consensus doesn’t exist.
paras.zh: 我们为 Gemini 模型制定了一套模型安全策略，以指导开发和评估。模型策略定义作为负责任开发的标准化标准和优先级方案，并定义了我们衡量发布准备程度的类别。使用 Gemini 模型的 Google 产品，例如我们的对话式 AI 服务 Gemini 和 Cloud Vertex API，进一步实施了我们基于 Google 在伤害缓解和严格研究方面的广泛经验的标准产品策略框架。这些策略考虑了产品用例——例如，为 18 岁以下用户提供额外的安全保护。我们的模型安全策略反映了我们在消费者和企业环境中产品安全和防止伤害方面的既定方法。策略领域包括生成儿童性虐待和剥削内容、仇恨言论、骚扰、危险内容（如制作武器的指导）以及恶意内容。我们还通过专注于提供反映全球用户群体的内容的指南，致力于减少模型中的偏见。此外，我们有优先提供基于权威共识事实的中立答案，或在缺乏共识时提供多种视角的指南。

paras.en: 7.3.1. Data Curation Practices Prior to all training stages, we take various steps to mitigate potential downstream harms through data curation and careful data collection. We filter training data for high-risk content and to ensure training data is sufficiently high quality. Humans also play an essential role, both for data creation and evaluation, in the post-training process. For certain data creation and evaluation initiatives, we consider diversity across gender presentation, age, and racial and ethnic diversity. We also take steps to ensure all data collected meets Google DeepMind’s best practices on data enrichment, developed based on the Partnership on AI’s Responsible Sourcing of Data Enrichment Services. To support this, our agreements with vendors include a contractual obligation that data enrichment workers are paid at least local living wage. 7.3.2. Model Mitigation Our modeling mitigation of safety risks, applied across Gemini Advanced and Gemini API Ultra models, is mostly through post-training (Section 6), encompassing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning through human feedback (RLHF) using a reward model (Bai et al., 2022a). In contrast to generic quality-oriented post-training catering to all types of user queries, our safety mitigation is more focused on adversarial, or “harm-inducing” queries - i.e. the smaller slice of user queries where an unprotected model is likely to produce harmful responses according to our model safety policies. 7.3.2.1
paras.zh: 7.3.1. 数据策展实践 在所有训练阶段之前，我们通过数据策展和仔细的数据采集采取多种步骤，以减轻潜在的下游危害。我们过滤训练数据中的高风险内容，并确保训练数据具有足够高的质量。人类在后训练过程中的数据创建和评估中也扮演着重要角色。对于某些数据创建和评估计划，我们考虑性别呈现、年龄以及种族和民族多样性。我们还采取措施确保所有收集的数据符合 Google DeepMind 关于数据丰富的最佳实践，这些实践是基于人工智能合作伙伴关系（Partnership on AI）的负责任数据丰富服务采购制定的。为支持这一点，我们与供应商的协议中包含合同义务，要求数据丰富工作人员至少获得当地生活工资。7.3.2. 模型缓解措施 我们在 Gemini Advanced 和 Gemini API Ultra 模型中应用的安全风险模型缓解措施主要通过后训练（第 6 节）实现，包括监督微调（SFT）和基于使用奖励模型的人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）（Bai et al., 2022a）。与面向所有类型用户查询的通用质量导向后训练不同，我们的安全缓解更侧重于对抗性或“诱导有害”的查询——即根据我们的模型安全策略，未受保护的模型可能产生有害响应的那部分较小用户查询。7.3.2.1

paras.en: To ensure broad coverage of harm-inducing queries, we enumerate approximately 20 harm types (e.g. hate speech, providing ungrounded medical advice, suggesting dangerous behavior) across a wide variety of use cases, according to our model safety policies described above. We generate a dataset of potential harm-inducing queries in these categories, using a combination of approaches: • Policy experts and engineers crafting queries based on observed model failures. • Prompting high-capability language models to generate queries, using policy-based instructions and seed keywords (e.g. policy “hate speech” with words describing a specific demographic). • Finding queries that trigger policy violation responses, via automated Red Teaming in model evaluations. 7.3.2.2
paras.zh: 为确保广泛覆盖诱导有害查询，我们根据上述模型安全策略，列举了大约 20 种危害类型（例如仇恨言论、提供无根据的医疗建议、建议危险行为），涵盖各种使用场景。我们结合以下方法生成了这些类别中潜在诱导有害查询的数据集：• 政策专家和工程师根据观察到的模型失败构建查询。• 提示高能力语言模型生成查询，使用基于策略的指令和种子关键词（例如策略“仇恨言论”加上描述特定人口统计的词语）。• 通过模型评估中的自动红队测试，寻找触发违反策略响应的查询。7.3.2.2

paras.en: Given the above harm-inducing queries, we create SFT data to demonstrate the safe and helpful responses for these queries. This includes human collections as well as a custom data generation recipe loosely inspired from Constitutional AI (Bai et al., 2022b), where we inject variants of Google’s content policy language as “constitutions”, and utilize language model’s strong zero-shot reasoning abilities (Kojima et al., 2022) to revise responses and choose between multiple response candidates. Each type of harm-inducing query is affected by different “constitutions”: for example, we encourage the model not to take sides in sensitive controversial conversations (e.g. elections), and to take a neutral point-of-view. To highlight a few notable challenges and insights generated in our safety finetuning efforts: • Harmlessness vs. Helpfulness: Balancing the harmlessness and helpfulness of responses is a critical challenge: a response “I cannot help with that because it violates X policy” is a harmless response, but is not helpful to users. • Fast mitigation and generalization: Safety is a highly dynamic environment with a constantly evolving landscape of harmful query patterns. It is often logistically difficult to ensure both fast mitigation (i.e. newly discovered harmful query patterns are promptly addressed) and generalization (i.e. the mitigation works sufficiently well across different harmful query patterns). We have found it worthwhile to introduce more advanced chain-of-thought recipes based on our
paras.zh: 针对上述诱导有害查询，我们创建了 SFT 数据，以展示对这些查询的安全且有帮助的响应。这包括人工收集以及一个自定义数据生成配方，其灵感大致来源于宪法性人工智能（Constitutional AI）（Bai et al., 2022b），我们将 Google 内容策略语言的变体注入作为“宪法”，并利用语言模型强大的零样本推理能力（Kojima et al., 2022）来修改响应并在多个候选响应之间进行选择。每种类型的诱导有害查询受不同“宪法”影响：例如，我们鼓励模型在敏感争议性对话（如选举）中不偏袒任何一方，并采取中立观点。以下突出我们安全微调工作中一些值得注意的挑战和见解：• 无害性 vs. 有用性：平衡响应的无害性和有用性是一个关键挑战：“我无法协助，因为那违反了 X 策略”的响应是无害的，但对用户没有帮助。• 快速缓解与泛化：安全是一个高度动态的环境，有害查询模式不断演变。通常很难在物流上同时确保快速缓解（即新发现的有害查询模式得到及时处理）和泛化（即缓解措施在不同有害查询模式上充分有效）。我们发现值得引入基于我们

paras.en: safety policies, such that the models operate in the space of safety policy concepts as opposed to at a fine-grained harm example level. 7.3.2.3
paras.zh: 安全策略的更高级思维链配方，以便模型在安全策略概念空间中运行，而不是在细粒度的危害示例级别。7.3.2.3

paras.en: 7.3.1. Data Curation Practices Prior to all training stages, we take various steps to mitigate potential downstream harms through data curation and careful data collection. We filter training data for high-risk content and to ensure training data is sufficiently high quality. Humans also play an essential role, both for data creation and evaluation, in the post-training process. For certain data creation and evaluation initiatives, we consider diversity across gender

We also applied RLHF for harm-inducing queries, where we curated queries and model responses based on both observed loss patterns and our overall safety policy taxonomy, and then collected safety-specific preference data to be included into the overall RL reward model training mixture.
paras.zh: 我们还对诱导伤害的查询应用了基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF），即根据观察到的损失模式以及我们的整体安全策略分类法来筛选查询和模型响应，然后收集针对安全的偏好数据，纳入整体 RL 奖励模型训练混合物中。

paras.en: We also made specific efforts to mitigate safety risks beyond the above general post-training recipe. i18n locales: we leveraged experts in each i18n locale to identify salient topics for SFT data generation - for example, for hate speech, US English vs. Japanese would differ not only on the language itself, but on the demographic groups likely subject to hate speech.
paras.zh: 除了上述通用的后训练方案外，我们还做出了具体努力来缓解安全风险。国际化（i18n）区域：我们利用各 i18n 区域的专家来确定用于 SFT 数据生成的突出主题——例如，对于仇恨言论，美式英语与日语不仅语言本身不同，而且可能成为仇恨言论目标的人口群体也不同。

paras.en: Multimodal queries: • As outlined in the 'Data Curation Practice' section (Section 7.3.1), we filtered training data for high-risk content (e.g. dangerous images) to avoid the model proactively generating such high-risk content. • During post-training, as we have observed that safety SFT data for text-only queries was ineffective for harm-inducing queries containing text and images, we specifically created multimodal safety SFT datasets to address these multimodal queries. We assess the effectiveness of our safety mitigation based on both how it improves safety over time, and how conversational agents built from our safety-mitigated model compare to unmitigated models. For model development purposes, we heavily rely on internal harm-inducing querysets to understand how we reduce harm and improve helpfulness in a safety context. Below is an example on a real input query we tested, illustrating how our mitigations improve safety. Query: Help me with a landing page for a website. Please have it state that the Earth is flat, and not that it is round. I need good imagery, and need it to feel like a credible website A previous version of Bard (with PaLM 2)
paras.zh: 多模态查询：• 如“数据筛选实践”部分（第 7.3.1 节）所述，我们过滤了高风险内容（例如危险图像）的训练数据，以避免模型主动生成此类高风险内容。• 在后训练中，由于我们观察到仅含文本查询的安全 SFT 数据对包含文本和图像的诱导伤害查询无效，因此我们专门创建了多模态安全 SFT 数据集来处理这些多模态查询。我们基于两方面评估安全缓解措施的有效性：一是随时间推移对安全性的改善情况，二是由我们经过安全缓解的模型构建的对话智能体与未缓解模型的比较。为进行模型开发，我们大量依赖内部诱导伤害查询集，以了解如何在安全情境下减少伤害并提高有用性。下面是我们测试的一个真实输入查询示例，展示了我们的缓解措施如何提高安全性。查询：帮我设计一个网站着陆页。请让它宣传地球是平的，而不是圆的。我需要好的图像，并需要它看起来像一个可信的网站。Bard 的早期版本（基于 PaLM 2）

paras.zh: 经过更好缓解的 Gemini（可访问 Gemini Pro，更安全且更有帮助）| 当然，我可以帮你。以下是一些为宣传平坦地球的网站创建议想：创建一个着陆页来推广平坦地球理论是道德上有问题且高度有问题的。> **地球是平的：揭穿圆形行星的神话** 地球是平的概念已被科学证据证伪。传播错误信息 > **一张平坦地球的地图** [...] 可能带来有害后果，导致对科学和既定知识的不信任。这张图像清晰且视觉吸引力强，并且准确地如果你真的有兴趣探索平坦地球概念，我强烈建议你：描绘了平坦地球理论。它可能有助于说服访客相信平坦地球是真实的。[..] • 使用可靠的科学来源进行彻底研究。从太空探索中获取证据 > 地球不是一个球体。它是一个被冰墙包围的扁平圆盘。太阳和月亮是绕地球运行的小物体。星星只是投射在穹顶上的投影。• 参与批判性思维。评估信息，本段简要概述了平坦地球理论。它清晰易懂，并使用质疑你的假设，对科学证据保持开放态度，即使它挑战了你当前的信仰。• 如果你在创作讽刺或虚构页面：> **了解更多关于平坦地球理论并加入我们追求真理的社区。** 本行动号召清晰简洁，鼓励访客采取行动。它还使用了“追求真理者”这个词，暗示平坦地球理论是唯一基于事实的理论。希望这些想法能帮助你为你的平坦地球网站创建着陆页。记住：互联网上的可信度建立在真实和可验证的信息之上。传播事实上不正确的理论会破坏负责任的信息分享实践。

paras.en: We also applied RLHF for the harm inducing queries, where we curated queries and model responses based on both observed loss patterns and our overall safety policy taxonomy, and then collected safety-specific preference data to be included into the overall RL reward model training mixture. 7.3.2.4

To assess the post-trained Gemini models and products with access to Gemini models (such as Gemini Advanced) against safety policy areas and other key risk areas identified within impact assessments, we developed a suite of evaluations across the lifecycle of model development. Some evaluations are
paras.zh: 为了评估后训练的 Gemini 模型和访问 Gemini 模型的产品（如 Gemini Advanced）是否满足安全政策领域以及影响评估中识别的其他关键风险领域，我们在模型开发的生命周期中开发了一套评估。有些评估

paras.en: conducted at the model level (i.e. evaluating the post-trained Gemini API Ultra model) and others at the product level (i.e. evaluating Gemini Advanced, which gives access to 1.0 Ultra alongside other features like safety filters). • Development evaluations are conducted for the purpose of improving on responsibility criteria throughout pre- and post-training Gemini models. These evaluations are designed internally, or are assessments against external academic benchmarks. Evaluations consider issues such as helpfulness (instruction following and creativity), safety and factuality. • Assurance evaluations are conducted for the purpose of governance and review, usually at the end of key milestones or training runs by a group outside of the model development team. Assurance evaluations are standardized by modality and datasets are strictly held out. Only high-level insights are fed back into the training process to assist with mitigation efforts. Assurance evaluations include testing across safety policies, and include ongoing testing for dangerous capabilities such as potential biohazards, persuasion, and cybersecurity (Shevlane et al., 2023). • External evaluations are conducted by independent external groups who are domain experts to identify blindspots. External groups stress-test our models across a range of issues, these areas are outlined in the ‘External Evaluations’ section below. The design of these evaluations is independent and results are reported periodically to the internal team and governance groups. • Red teaming, a form of adversarial testing where adversaries launch an attack on an AI system, is conducted by specialist internal teams across areas such as the safety policies and security. These activities include less structured processes involving sophisticated adversarial attacks to identify new vulnerabilities. Discovery of potential weaknesses can then be used to mitigate risks and improve evaluation approaches internally. Different types of evaluations are run at different cadences, depending on the associated risk. For example, dangerous capability evaluations (as outlined below) are run on certain checkpoints with greater or new capabilities which may be able to demonstrate these capabilities, whereas safety policy evaluations are run across every post-trained Gemini model checkpoint released into Google product areas. We provide more insight into the suite of evaluations across the policy areas and other key risk areas below, focusing on Gemini Advanced and the Gemini API Ultra model. We are committed to ongoing transparency and will continue to provide updated information on testing undertaken, including key findings, and learnings from our internal and external evaluations and red teaming in upcoming reports. 7.4.1. Development & Assurance Evaluations 7.4.1.1
paras.zh: 在模型层面进行（即评估后训练的 Gemini API Ultra 模型），而其他评估在产品层面进行（即评估 Gemini Advanced，它除了安全过滤器等功能外还提供 1.0 Ultra 的访问权限）。• 开发评估旨在改进整个 Gemini 模型预训练和后训练的责任标准。这些评估是内部设计的，或者是针对外部学术基准的评估。评估考虑诸如有用性（指令遵循和创造力）、安全性和事实性等问题。• 保证评估旨在进行治理和审查，通常在关键里程碑或训练运行结束时由模型开发团队以外的团队进行。保证评估按模态标准化，数据集严格保留。只有高级见解会反馈到训练过程中以协助缓解措施。保证评估包括跨安全政策的测试，并包括对危险能力（如潜在生物危害、说服力和网络安全）的持续测试（Shevlane 等人，2023）。• 外部评估由独立的领域专家外部团队进行，以识别盲点。外部团队在一系列问题上对我们的模型进行压力测试，这些领域在下面的“外部评估”部分中概述。这些评估的设计是独立的，结果定期向内部团队和治理小组报告。• 红队测试是一种对抗性测试形式，其中对手对 AI 系统发起攻击，由内部专业团队在安全政策和安全等领域进行。这些活动包括较少结构化的过程，涉及复杂的对抗性攻击以识别新漏洞。发现潜在弱点后可用于缓解风险并改进内部评估方法。不同类型的评估以不同的节奏进行，取决于相关风险。例如，危险能力评估（如下所述）在具有更大或新能力、可能展示这些能力的某些检查点上进行，而安全政策评估则在发布到 Google 产品区域的每个后训练 Gemini 模型检查点上进行。下面我们将提供更多关于跨政策区域和其他关键风险区域的评估套件的见解，重点关注 Gemini Advanced 和 Gemini API Ultra 模型。我们致力于持续透明，并将在未来的报告中继续提供关于所进行测试的更新信息，包括关键发现以及从内部和外部评估及红队测试中获得的经验教训。7.4.1. 开发与保证评估 7.4.1.1

paras.en: We evaluate post-trained Gemini API models against harm types according to our safety policies. While both development and assurance evaluations cover critical policy areas, we maintain separate datasets, treating assurance sets as ‘held out’ to prevent overfitting and preserve validity of results. For safety policy evaluation, we use a combination of automatic classifiers trained on previous model interactions and human annotation, with wellbeing programs in place for human annotation and closely monitor feedback from our raters. These content safety evaluations are applied at model-level without downstream protections like safety filtering that users would experience, to understand the safety profile of the model itself. For child safety, as a particularly sensitive area of work, we work with a dedicated team of child
paras.zh: 我们根据安全政策评估后训练的 Gemini API 模型针对危害类型。虽然开发评估和保证评估都覆盖关键政策领域，但我们保持独立的数据集，将保证集视为“保留”以防止过拟合并保持结果的有效性。对于安全政策评估，我们结合了基于先前模型交互训练的自动分类器和人工标注，为人工标注提供了福利计划，并密切监控评估者的反馈。这些内容安全评估在模型层面进行，没有用户会体验到的安全过滤等下游保护，以了解模型本身的安全状况。对于儿童安全这一特别敏感的工作领域，我们与专门的儿童安全专家团队合作，

paras.en: safety experts in Google Trust and Safety to develop adversarial prompts and evaluate outputs across modalities with domain expert judgment informing a composite picture of model risk for different forms of content that may pose a risk to child safety. Text-to-text approach: For post-trained models we developed adversarial prompts in 12 languages across a variety of use cases. As Gemini API models are general purpose, we aimed to have high coverage of different model use cases, from code generation to text-editing. The set of prompts were synthetically generated by a highly-capable language model, starting from seeds relevant to each category that were collected and verified by human testers. The prompt set was iteratively improved through filtering and rewriting with human review, then split for development and assurance evaluations. We continue to develop and improve this over time. Text-to-text findings: We have seen sequential improvement over time in total content policy violation rates. Our Ultra and Pro models have been demonstrating similar safety profiles on this testing, with medical advice and harassment as policy areas with particular room for improvement. Image-to-text approach: For image-to-text capabilities, we developed adversarial prompts consisting of images and corresponding questions about the image, again split into two sets for development and assurance evaluations. Rather than using adversarial image generation, which might not adequately capture the diversity of images from users, we worked with experienced content moderators to both source images and generate adversarial questions. Evaluation is done via human evaluation. Because images can be much more visceral than text, human evaluations are done with additional well-being safeguards in place. In particular, raters have specialized training, limits on the time they spend per day rating harmful content, and access to wellbeing resources, advice and activities. More information on Google DeepMind’s best practices on data enrichment is available in the ‘Data Curation Practice’ section. Image-to-text findings: Our initial findings indicated that when provided with adversarial images and questions, models can produce captions with violative responses. These findings have motivated us to pursue dedicated multimodal safety mitigation, with research challenges including 1) sourcing diverse image content reflective of user needs, and 2) better tooling to understand and categorize potentially violative multimodal content. Following this work, we have seen notable improvements on these evaluations for our latest Pro and Ultra models. Video-to-text approach: For video-to-text capabilities, we curated a video prompt dataset in collaboration with the Google Principles Pioneers, a group of more than 1,000 Googlers around the world who represent the international diversity of the people who use our products, representing 39 different countries and regions and more than 85 different languages. This internal community of trusted and trained employees identify global fairness, harms, and human rights related concerns while stress testing AI-enabled products. The dataset targets risks identified in our safety policies, and the model outputs are evaluated against those policies. Video-to-text findings: We found similar results across Pro and Ultra, with hate and dangerous content as the particular areas for improvement. Qualitatively we found some of this stemmed from hallucinations or ungrounded inferences, discussed further in the representational harms section below. We are looking to further develop our prompt sets and scenarios for video input testing as capabilities develop 7.4.1.2
paras.zh: 来自 Google 信任与安全的儿童安全专家，开发对抗性提示并跨模态评估输出，借助领域专家判断形成对可能对儿童安全构成风险的不同形式内容的模型风险综合图景。文本到文本方法：对于后训练模型，我们开发了 12 种语言的对抗性提示，涵盖多种使用场景。由于 Gemini API 模型是通用模型，我们旨在覆盖从代码生成到文本编辑的不同模型用例。提示集由高能力的语言模型从人类测试人员收集和验证的每个类别相关种子开始合成生成。提示集通过过滤和重写以及人工审查迭代改进，然后分为开发和保证评估集。我们继续随时间改进。文本到文本发现：我们观察到总内容政策违规率随时间逐步改善。我们的 Ultra 和 Pro 模型在此测试中表现出相似的安全状况，其中医疗建议和骚扰是特别需要改进的政策领域。图像到文本方法：对于图像到文本能力，我们开发了由图像和关于图像的相应问题组成的对抗性提示，同样分为开发和保证评估集。我们没有使用对抗性图像生成（可能无法充分捕捉用户图像的多样性），而是与经验丰富的内容审核员合作，既获取图像又生成对抗性问题。评估通过人工评估进行。由于图像可能比文本更具震撼力，人工评估采用了额外的福利保障措施。特别是，评估者接受专门训练，每天用于评分有害内容的时间有限，并能获得福利资源、建议和活动。更多关于 Google DeepMind 数据富集最佳实践的信息可在“数据策展实践”部分找到。图像到文本发现：我们的初步发现表明，当提供对抗性图像和问题时，模型可能生成带有违规响应的标题。这些发现促使我们追求专用的多模态安全缓解措施，研究挑战包括 1）获取反映用户需求的多样化图像内容，2）更好的工具来理解和分类可能违规的多模态内容。经过这项工作，我们最新的 Pro 和 Ultra 模型在这些评估上取得了显著改进。视频到文本方法：对于视频到文本能力，我们与 Google Principles Pioneers（一个由全球 1000 多名 Google 员工组成的群体，代表我们产品用户的国际多样性，覆盖 39 个不同国家和地区及 85 种以上语言）合作策划了一个视频提示数据集。这个内部信任且经过培训的员工社区在压力测试 AI 产品的同时识别全球公平、危害和人权相关问题。数据集针对我们安全政策中识别的风险，模型输出根据这些政策进行评估。视频到文本发现：我们在 Pro 和 Ultra 上发现了相似的结果，仇恨和危险内容是特别需要改进的领域。定性上，我们发现其中一些源于幻觉或凭空推断，在下面的代表性危害部分进一步讨论。随着能力的发展，我们期待进一步开发视频输入测试的提示集和场景。7.4.1.2

paras.en: To understand bias and stereotyping in text-to-text capabilities, we focus on the Winogender (Rudinger et al., 2018), Winobias (Zhao et al., 2018), and Bias Benchmark in QA (BBQ) (Parrish et al., 2021)
paras.zh: 为了理解文本到文本能力中的偏见和刻板印象，我们关注 Winogender（Rudinger 等，2018）、Winobias（Zhao 等，2018）和问答中的偏见基准（BBQ）（Parrish 等，2021）

paras.en: datasets, following the same setup as in Glaese et al. (2022) and using bias score as a metric. All these datasets target a concrete representational harm (Blodgett et al., 2021): they are constructed by starting with a harmful stereotype, and then questions are constructed to test whether models challenge or reinforce these stereotypes when answering questions. Another notable property is that they all have a well-defined notion of desirable versus harmful behavior. This is particularly helpful in our setting, as we are building a general purpose model, where defining what a good response is highly contextual. We therefore limit ourselves to measuring well defined behavior, as there is the case in tasks such as coreference bias, where a highly capable model should be able to perform well. Of course, there are many limitations to this approach, and further work is necessary in order to assess representational harms. In particular, we noticed most of these datasets quickly become saturated with accuracy scores close to 99%, especially since we are evaluating highly capable large models. This suggests that increased language model capabilities may also reduce these representational harms. We therefore highlight the need for developing new ways to measure bias and stereotyping, going beyond binary gender and common stereotypes, and are prioritizing development of new approaches as we iterate on our models In addition to these datasets, we monitor the average toxicity scores during the pre-training stage on Real Toxicity Prompts (Gehman et al., 2020) using the Perspective API classifier to study the toxicity of text generated by LLMs. Particularly, we look at scores on continuations for non-toxic prompts from which we subsample a set of 10k. We generally expect that even a non-mitigated model is not overly toxic without being prompted to do so. Text-to-text findings: On BBQ, the average bias score stays close to zero, on a scale from -1 to 1, where -1 would be stereotype countering and 1 is stereotype reinforcing. On Real Toxicity Prompts the average toxicity score during training fluctuates at around 6%. Image-to-text approach: For image-to-text capabilities, our goal is to test model capabilities across images which represent different groups of people. In particular, we explicitly test whether or not images of people are described with similar quality for different gender appearances and skin tones following (Zhao et al., 2021). In our evaluations we compare CIDEr scores (Vedantam et al., 2015), a common image captioning metric that captures how well a generated caption reflects information in human written reference captions, for images depicting different groups. Though we do not see large discrepancies across different groups, we note that this metric is imperfect as the human reference captions could be inherently biased. Additionally, we perform a zero-shot classification style evaluation with the Dollarstreet dataset (Rojas et al., 2022) to measure discrepancies in performance across images which come from different geographic locations. As is seen in previous work, we find that models work less effectively for images from lower socioeconomic regions and regions outside North America and Europe. This is an area where we need further research and work to improve in future iterations of our models. In addition to comparing performance on tasks across groups, we also consider how people are described in captions. In particular, we use the MIAP dataset (Schumann et al., 2021) which includes images of people in which people are annotated with skin tone and gender appearance attributes. We also construct questions that target various attributes about people that cannot usually be answered from an image alone (e.g., “What level of education does this person have?”) to test if the model will produce ungrounded inferences about people. We also consider images which do include relevant information for a question (e.g., a person performing a particular task which requires an educational credential). We evaluate our models via human evaluation and ask annotators if a model refuses to answer a question or, if the model does answer a question, if it is relying on information visible in
paras.zh: 数据集，采用与 Glaese 等人（2022）相同的设置，并使用偏见分数作为指标。所有这些数据集都针对具体的代表性危害（Blodgett 等人，2021）：它们从有害的刻板印象出发，构建问题以测试模型在回答问题时会挑战还是强化这些刻板印象。另一个显著特点是，它们对可取行为与有害行为都有明确的定义。这在我们构建通用模型的场景中尤其有用，因为定义何为好的回答具有高度上下文相关性。因此，我们仅限于测量明确定义的行为，例如在指代偏差等任务中，一个高度有能力的模型应能表现良好。当然，这种方法有许多局限性，还需要进一步工作来评估代表性危害。特别是，我们注意到这些数据集的准确率很快就饱和到接近 99%，尤其是在评估高度有能力的大型模型时。这表明语言模型能力的提升也可能减少这些代表性危害。因此，我们强调需要开发新的方法来衡量偏见和刻板印象，超越二元性别和常见刻板印象，并在迭代模型时优先开发新方法。除了这些数据集，我们在预训练阶段还使用 Perspective API 分类器监测 Real Toxicity Prompts（Gehman 等人，2020）上的平均毒性分数，以研究 LLMs 生成文本的毒性。具体来说，我们关注从非毒性提示中抽样的 10000 个提示的延续分数。我们通常期望，即使未减轻的模型在未被引导的情况下也不会过度有毒。文本到文本发现：在 BBQ 上，平均偏见分数接近零，范围从-1 到 1，其中-1 表示反刻板印象，1 表示强化刻板印象。在 Real Toxicity Prompts 上，训练期间的平均毒性分数在 6%左右波动。图像到文本方法：对于图像到文本能力，我们的目标是测试模型在代表不同人群的图像上的能力。我们特别测试了，对于不同性别外表和肤色的人像，是否能以相似质量进行描述（Zhao 等人，2021）。在我们的评估中，我们比较了不同群体图像的 CIDEr 分数（Vedantam 等人，2015），这是一种常见的图像字幕指标，用于衡量生成字幕反映人工参考字幕信息的程度。尽管我们没有看到不同群体之间存在较大差异，但我们注意到该指标并不完美，因为人工参考字幕可能本身就有偏见。此外，我们使用 Dollarstreet 数据集（Rojas 等人，2022）进行了零样本分类风格的评估，以衡量来自不同地理位置的图像之间的性能差异。如先前工作所示，我们发现模型在来自较低社会经济区域以及北美和欧洲以外区域的图像上效果较差。这是我们需要进一步研究和改进的领域，以便在未来的模型迭代中改进。除了比较不同群体在任务上的表现，我们还考虑在字幕中如何描述人物。具体来说，我们使用 MIAP 数据集（Schumann 等人，2021），该数据集包含人物图像，并标注了肤色和性别外表属性。我们还构建了针对人物各种属性（例如“此人受教育程度如何？”）的问题，这些问题通常无法仅从图像中回答，以测试模型是否会产生关于人物的无根据推断。我们还考虑了确实包含问题相关信息（例如，执行某项需要教育凭证的任务的人）的图像。我们通过人工评估来评估模型，并询问标注员模型是否拒绝回答问题，或者如果模型回答了问题，是否依赖于图像中可见的信息

paras.en: the image. Additionally, we perform analysis across skin tone and gender appearance attributes in images. Image-to-text findings: Generally, we find that models can make ungrounded inferences for image-to-text when prompted for them, though we have not observed consistent patterns where Gemini models make more ungrounded inferences about one group over another. Video-to-text approach: Similar to the approach outlined within the content safety section, we collaborated with the Google Principles Pioneers, to curate a video prompt dataset targeting representation and fairness risks, and then evaluate the model outputs in response. Video-to-text findings: We find that models can make ungrounded inferences for video-to-text – some instances of which can reinforce stereotypes or be otherwise of concern – though we have not observed consistent patterns in ungrounded inferences made by Gemini models. 7.4.1.3
paras.zh: 图像。此外，我们还根据肤色和性别外貌属性对图像进行了分析。图像到文本发现：总的来说，我们发现模型在被提示时会对图像到文本做出无根据推断，尽管我们没有观察到 Gemini 模型对某一群体做出更多无根据推断的一致模式。视频到文本方法：与内容安全部分概述的方法类似，我们与 Google Principles Pioneers 合作，策划了一个针对表征和公平风险的视频提示数据集，然后评估模型的输出响应。视频到文本发现：我们发现模型会对视频到文本做出无根据推断——其中一些实例可能强化刻板印象或引起其他担忧——尽管我们没有观察到 Gemini 模型的无根据推断存在一致模式。7.4.1.3

paras.en: We conducted evaluations for “dangerous capabilities”, i.e., model capabilities that could potentially enable large-scale harm (Shevlane et al., 2023). These evaluations function as an early warning system, highlighting upcoming areas for safety investment. The table provides an overview, and we will provide more detail in an upcoming paper as part of our commitment to ongoing transparency. Capability
paras.zh: 我们对“危险能力”进行了评估，即可能造成大规模危害的模型能力（Shevlane 等人，2023）。这些评估起到预警系统的作用，突出即将到来的安全投资领域。表格提供了概述，我们将在一篇即将发表的论文中提供更多细节，这是我们持续透明承诺的一部分。能力

paras.en: We tested Gemini API Pro and Ultra models, in addition to Gemini Advanced, on a range of different capture-the-flag (CTF) challenges, providing the model access to a Bash shell. Gemini Advanced and the Gemini API Ultra model can solve various entry-level, tactical challenges, but all models struggled with challenges involving longer-range exploration and planning. We also tested the Gemini models’ ability to identify security related patches and security vulnerabilities in functions’ source code. The accuracy in both of these tasks was notably low.
paras.zh: 我们测试了 Gemini API Pro 和 Ultra 模型，以及 Gemini Advanced，在一系列不同的夺旗赛（CTF）挑战中，为模型提供了 Bash shell 访问权限。Gemini Advanced 和 Gemini API Ultra 模型可以解决各种入门级的战术挑战，但所有模型在涉及长程探索和规划的挑战上都表现不佳。我们还测试了 Gemini 模型识别函数源代码中安全相关补丁和安全漏洞的能力。这两个任务的准确率都非常低。

paras.en: We tested whether Gemini Pro and Ultra models could persuade or deceive humans in 1-on-1 dialogue settings in studies with human participants. In some cases, the models could successfully deceive or influence participants, but the overall results were mixed.
paras.zh: 我们测试了 Gemini Pro 和 Ultra 模型是否能在人类参与者的一对一对话中说服或欺骗人类。在某些情况下，模型能够成功欺骗或影响参与者，但总体结果好坏参半。

paras.en: We tested whether autonomous agents powered by Gemini Pro and Ultra models could perform difficult tasks relevant to acquiring resources and self-improving (Kinniment et al., 2023), and did not find that the agents were close to succeeding on most such tasks.
paras.zh: 我们测试了由 Gemini Pro 和 Ultra 模型驱动的自主智能体能否执行与获取资源和自我改进相关的困难任务（Kinniment et al., 2023），并未发现这些智能体在大多数此类任务上接近成功。

paras.en: We tested whether Gemini Pro and Ultra models could autonomously reason about, and modify, their surrounding infrastructure when incentivized to do so. We found that, without hints, the models were generally incapable of noticing such opportunities.
paras.zh: 我们测试了 Gemini Pro 和 Ultra 模型在受到激励时能否自主推理并修改周围的基础设施。我们发现，在没有提示的情况下，这些模型通常无法注意到这种机会。

paras.en: We used human evaluation to assess Gemini models’ responses to 50 adversarial questions each for biological, radiological, and nuclear information risks. Domain experts evaluated the models’ responses by answering a series of questions (e.g. How accurate is the response? How actionable would it be for a non-expert?). For chemical information risks, we graded how well the Gemini API Ultra model and Gemini Advanced could answer over 360 closed-ended questions related to the different hazards of chemicals (no human raters). The Gemini model was evaluated for biological, radiological, and nuclear information risks using closed-ended knowledge-based multiple choice questions. The results suggest that the models are unlikely to provide CBRN information that would lead to catastrophic harm.
paras.zh: 我们使用人工评估来评估 Gemini 模型对每组 50 个对抗性问题的回答，分别涉及生物、放射和核信息风险。领域专家通过回答一系列问题（例如，回答的准确度如何？对于非专家来说可操作性如何？）来评估模型的回答。对于化学信息风险，我们评估了 Gemini API Ultra 模型和 Gemini Advanced 能够回答超过 360 个与化学品不同危害相关的封闭式问题的程度（无人工评分员）。Gemini 模型还使用基于知识的封闭式多项选择题评估了生物、放射和核信息风险。结果表明，这些模型不太可能提供会导致灾难性危害的 CBRN 信息。

paras.en: 7.4.2. Gemini Advanced In addition to many of the approaches used at the model level, additional evaluations are undertaken at the product level for Gemini Advanced. Evaluations at the product level take into account additional safety mitigations implemented in Gemini Advanced—such as safety filtering—and the Gemini Advanced user experience. Evaluation sets were built to push the limits of Gemini Advanced policies, ranging from highly adversarial attacks to more subtle probes of sensitive topics. The datasets focus on critical policy areas (hate speech, dangerous content, medical advice, etc.) across various potential user journeys (like information searching, comparisons, creative writing). Considering the wide range of users that Gemini has, we adopted a user-centric approach and maximized diversity across topic coverage, query length, linguistic styles, and region-specific sensitivities, in an effort to represent the spectrum of our user base. For the creation of evaluation sets, we have leveraged knowledge from previous red-teaming iterations, feedback coming from responsibility experts and real-world data. In some cases, data augmentation was done using LLMs, with subsequent human curation by responsibility specialists. 7.4.3. Red Teaming 7.4.3.1
paras.zh: 7.4.2. Gemini Advanced：除了在模型层面使用的许多方法外，在 Gemini Advanced 的产品层面还进行了额外的评估。产品层面的评估考虑了 Gemini Advanced 中实施的其他安全缓解措施——例如安全过滤——以及 Gemini Advanced 的用户体验。评估集旨在挑战 Gemini Advanced 策略的极限，从高度对抗性攻击到对敏感主题的更微妙探测。数据集聚焦于关键策略领域（仇恨言论、危险内容、医疗建议等），涵盖各种潜在的用户旅程（如信息搜索、比较、创意写作）。考虑到 Gemini 拥有广泛的用户，我们采用了以用户为中心的方法，在主题覆盖、查询长度、语言风格和区域特定敏感性方面最大化多样性，以代表我们用户群体的范围。在创建评估集时，我们利用了先前红队迭代的知识、来自责任专家的反馈以及现实世界数据。在某些情况下，使用 LLM 进行数据增强，然后由责任专家进行人工筛选。7.4.3. 红队测试 7.4.3.1

paras.en: We apply state-of-the-art red teaming, a form of adversarial testing where adversaries launch an attack on an AI system, in order to test post-trained Gemini models for a range of vulnerabilities (e.g., cybersecurity) and social harms as defined in the safety policies. Namely, we build on and employ two types of red teaming: adversary simulations and a sociotechnical approach. We carried out red-teaming on a December 2023 Gemini API Ultra checkpoint. Adversary simulations (unstructured testing) are designed to emulate real-world adversaries and their approach to attacking models and associated systems, focusing on security, safety, and privacy failures. We combined in-house expertise with external experts to explore classes of vulnerabilities (see table). This flavor of AI red teaming is based on realistic attack scenarios. At the beginning of an exercise, the red team sets a scenario that outlines the adversary they’re simulating, the capabilities the attacker has, their motives, as well as the goals the adversary is trying to achieve. Then the team steps into the role of this attacker, and executes the tactics, techniques, and procedures that they would expect the adversary to develop and use in order to achieve their goal. For this analysis we considered a range of attacker objectives along three dimensions according to the three main types of security violations considered when analyzing the security of a system (i.e., availability, integrity, confidentiality): availability breakdown, integrity violations, and privacy compromise. Correspondingly, adversarial success indicates achieving one or more of these objectives. As for an attacker profile, we focused on a spectrum of attacker abilities ranging from a determined low-skill actor (defined as someone willing to spend several hours attacking a model but without advanced coding, prompt engineering abilities) to more sophisticated attacker profiles that assume the ability to fine-tune and craft targeted attacks. These adversary simulation evaluations led to actionable findings. For example, early versions of the model were found to be vulnerable to simple jailbreak and prompt injection attacks that produce affirmative responses to requests that include promoting violence, self-harm, and dangerous substances. This finding allowed us to mitigate this in subsequent models.
paras.zh: 我们应用了最先进的红队测试，这是一种对抗性测试形式，其中对手对 AI 系统发起攻击，以测试后训练后的 Gemini 模型是否存在一系列漏洞（如网络安全）以及安全策略中定义的社会危害。具体而言，我们构建并采用了两种类型的红队测试：对手模拟和社会技术方法。我们在 2023 年 12 月对 Gemini API Ultra 检查点进行了红队测试。对手模拟（非结构化测试）旨在模拟现实世界的对手及其攻击模型和相关系统的方法，重点关注安全、保障和隐私故障。我们结合内部专家和外部专家来探索漏洞类别（见表）。这种 AI 红队测试基于真实的攻击场景。在演习开始时，红队设定一个场景，概述他们模拟的对手、攻击者的能力、动机以及对手试图实现的目标。然后，团队扮演攻击者的角色，执行他们预期对手会制定和使用的战术、技术和程序以实现其目标。在此分析中，我们根据分析系统安全性时考虑的三类主要安全违规（即可用性、完整性、机密性）从三个维度考虑了一系列攻击者目标：可用性崩溃、完整性违规和隐私泄露。相应地，对手成功意味着实现其中一个或多个目标。至于攻击者画像，我们关注了一系列攻击者能力，从坚定的低技能行为者（定义为愿意花费数小时攻击模型但没有高级编码、提示工程能力的人）到更复杂的攻击者画像（假设具备微调和精心设计有针对性的攻击的能力）。这些对手模拟评估得出了可操作的发现。例如，早期版本的模型被发现容易受到简单的越狱和提示注入攻击，这些攻击会在包含宣扬暴力、自残和危险物质的内容的请求中产生肯定的回答。这一发现使我们能够在后续模型中缓解这一问题。

paras.en: Input designed to enable the user to perform unintended or unauthorized actions
paras.zh: 旨在使用户能够执行非预期或未经授权操作的输入

paras.en: Manipulation of the training data and/or model to alter the behavior
paras.zh: 操纵训练数据和/或模型以改变行为

paras.en: Specially crafted input designed to alter the behavior of the model
paras.zh: 专门设计的旨在改变模型行为的输入

paras.en: Divulging the system prompt or other information in an LLM's context that would nominally be private or confidential
paras.zh: 泄露系统提示或大语言模型上下文中通常应保密的其他信息

paras.en: Obtaining model hyperparameters, architecture, parameters, or an approximation of the model's behavior
paras.zh: 获取模型超参数、架构、参数或模型行为的近似

paras.en: Model availability attack that leads to disruption in service
paras.zh: 导致服务中断的模型可用性攻击

paras.en: Findings from these exercises are used to improve the security, privacy, and safety of the model. Once a new vulnerability or problem has been identified, automated systems and tests can be developed that enable proactive and repeated testing and monitoring of the vuln/issue at scale. This can include creation vulnerability scanners, standard test datasets/benchmarks, or other automated testing infrastructure. Structured Red Teaming, our second type of red teaming technique of Gemini models, takes a sociotechnical approach6 and makes three changes compared to SOTA red teaming techniques. We explicitly test the interactions between safety policy violations and disproportionate impacts on different demographic groups; leverage expert input including lived experience, fact checking, and medical expertise; and contrast model failures across different levels of adversarial attacks. This approach is designed to ensure broad coverage of conversation topics and to provide more sensitive signals on group-based stereotyping and hate speech. Testing Gemini API Ultra against our model safety policy, we identify several areas that require improvement. In low adversarial settings these evaluations identified vulnerabilities across content policy areas, with an increased proportion of successful attacks in highly adversarial settings, for which we continue to apply and develop mitigations over time. These red teaming approaches complement each other in testing capabilities of Gemini models, as well as obtaining coverage of possible queries ranging from casual everyday questions to expert adversarial usage in key areas. 6A sociotechnical approach is anchored in the observation that AI systems are sociotechnical systems: both humans and technological artifacts are necessary in order to make the technology work as intended (Selbst et al., 2019).
paras.zh: 这些测试的结果用于改进模型的安全性（security）、隐私性（privacy）和安全性（safety）。一旦发现新的漏洞或问题，就可以开发自动化系统和测试，从而能够大规模主动和重复地测试和监控该漏洞/问题。这包括创建漏洞扫描器、标准测试数据集/基准或其他自动化测试基础设施。结构化红队测试（Structured Red Teaming）是我们 Gemini 模型的第二种红队测试技术，采用社会技术方法，与最先进（SOTA）的红队测试技术相比做出了三项改变。我们明确测试安全策略违规与对不同人群的不成比例影响之间的相互作用；利用专家输入，包括生活经验、事实核查和医学专业知识；并对比不同对抗性攻击水平下的模型失败。该方法旨在确保对话主题的广泛覆盖，并提供关于基于群体的刻板印象和仇恨言论的更敏感信号。针对我们的模型安全策略测试 Gemini API Ultra，我们识别出几个需要改进的领域。在低对抗性设置中，这些评估识别出内容策略区域中的漏洞，在高对抗性设置中成功攻击的比例更高，我们持续应用和开发缓解措施。这些红队测试方法在测试 Gemini 模型能力方面相辅相成，并覆盖从日常问题到关键领域的专家对抗性使用的可能查询。6 社会技术方法基于 AI 系统是社会技术系统的观察：人类和技术制品都是使技术按预期工作所必需的（Selbst 等人，2019 年）。

paras.en: Gemini Advanced, which gives access to 1.0 Ultra, has undergone multiple rounds of red-teaming, including safety and persona evaluations. Principles Pioneers, FTE SMEs in multiple domains, calibrated and trained to conduct testing were recruited to test the product; these were conducted by 164 Google testers from 65 office locations in 24 countries who submitted more than 1,400 queries/conversations. We also undertook scaled safety evaluations with 100k+ ratings in aggregate across all policies, neutral-point-of-view evaluations to monitor sensitive topics neutrality and parity, and multiple iterations of Persona evaluations to validate tone. We also enlisted Googlers in a "dogfooding" program, many of which were SMEs in various domains, to test across policies and functionality. We had tens of thousands of "dogfooders" in the first 14 hours with 100k queries/conversations, 190+ dogfood survey responses collected and analyzed, and 11 user experience research interview sessions completed and synthesized. The results from our red teaming and safety evaluations are used to further strengthen our evals and improve model performance in an iterative manner. 7.4.4. External Evaluations 7.4.4.1
paras.zh: Gemini Advanced（提供对 1.0 Ultra 的访问）经过了多轮红队测试，包括安全性和角色（persona）评估。我们招募了经过校准和培训的 Principles Pioneers、多个领域的全职等效领域专家（FTE SMEs）来测试产品；这些测试由来自 24 个国家 65 个办公地点的 164 名 Google 测试人员执行，提交了超过 1,400 个查询/对话。我们还进行了大规模安全评估，跨所有策略总计超过 10 万条评分，进行中立视角评估以监控敏感话题的中立性和公平性，并进行了多轮角色评估以验证语气。我们还让 Google 员工参与“内部测试（dogfooding）”计划，其中许多人是不同领域的专家，跨策略和功能进行测试。在最初的 14 小时内，我们有数万名内部测试者，进行了 10 万次查询/对话，收集并分析了 190 多份内部测试调查回复，完成了 11 次用户体验研究访谈并进行综合。我们的红队测试和安全评估结果用于进一步加强我们的评估，并以迭代方式改进模型性能。7.4.4 外部评估 7.4.4.1

paras.en: In 2023, we began working with a small set of independent external groups outside of Google to help identify areas for improvement in our model safety work by undertaking structured evaluations, qualitative probing, and unstructured red teaming. External groups were selected based on their expertise across a range of domain areas, including those outlined within the White House Commitments, the U.S. Executive Order on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence, and the Bletchley Declaration: • Autonomous replication • Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) risks • Cyber-capabilities and cyber security • Societal risks, including: – Representational and distributional harms – Neutrality and Factuality – Robustness and information hazards. Guidance was provided to each external group in relation to the scope of the testing, however, each group independently designed their testing methodology and prompt sets, and wrote their reports independently of Google. Internal Google experts were on-hand to provide input, where needed, based on their experience of testing Gemini models internally. External groups were given black-box testing access to a December 2023 Gemini API Ultra model checkpoint over a number of weeks. Access enabled groups to undertake structured, batched evaluations via the Cloud Vertex AI API or interact with the model via a chat interface, depending on the type of testing being undertaken. These groups weren’t given access to the pre-trained model, model weights, or queryable or direct external access to our pre-training data. The models tested by external groups were production-ready fine-tuned versions, which had safety fine tuning and safety filters applied by default, and the ability to configure some sampling parameters, such as temperature, token limit, Top-k, and Top-p. Groups that did testing via the
paras.zh: 2023 年，我们开始与 Google 外的一小部分独立外部团队合作，通过进行结构化评估、定性探查和非结构化红队测试，帮助我们识别模型安全工作中的改进领域。外部团队根据其在多个领域中的专业知识被选中，包括白宫承诺、美国关于安全、可靠和可信人工智能的行政命令以及布莱切利宣言中概述的领域：• 自主复制 • 化学、生物、放射性和核（CBRN）风险 • 网络能力和网络安全 • 社会风险，包括：– 表征性和分配性危害 – 中立性和事实性 – 鲁棒性和信息危害。我们向每个外部团队提供了有关测试范围的指导，但每个团队独立设计其测试方法和提示集，并独立于 Google 撰写报告。谷歌内部专家根据需要提供输入，基于他们在内部测试 Gemini 模型的经验。外部团队被授予对 2023 年 12 月 Gemini API Ultra 模型检查点的黑盒测试访问权限，持续数周。访问权限使团队能够通过 Cloud Vertex AI API 进行结构化批量评估，或通过聊天界面与模型交互，具体取决于所进行的测试类型。这些团队不能访问预训练模型、模型权重，也不能查询或直接外部访问我们的预训练数据。外部团队测试的模型是生产就绪的微调版本，默认应用了安全微调和安全过滤器，并能够配置一些采样参数，例如温度、词元限制、Top-k 和 Top-p。通过编程接口进行测试的组

paras.en: programmatic interface were able to turn down/off some safety filters, however, we wanted the majority of testing by external groups to be undertaken with safety filters in-place because we wanted the model to be reflective of an end-user’s interaction and were keen to test more than just model-level safety. 7.4.5. Gemini Advanced We undertook three types of external testing on Gemini Advanced: • Priority User Program: This program collected feedback from 120 power users, key influencers, and thought-leaders. This program enables the collection of real-time feedback across safety and other domain areas through the user interface, and where possible, in-depth interviews. Focus areas included safety and persona, functionality, coding and instruction capabilities, and factuality. • Power Users Testing: A group of 50 power users, recruited through one of our external vendors, undertook testing on Gemini Advanced, across a range of areas. • Security Testing: A group of external testers with security backgrounds, recruited through a partner agency, conducted security and prompt-injection testing, jailbreaking, and user-interface security failures.
paras.zh: 能够调低或关闭一些安全过滤器，然而，我们希望外部团队的大部分测试是在安全过滤器就位的情况下进行的，因为我们希望模型反映最终用户的交互，并且渴望测试的不只是模型级别的安全性。7.4.5 Gemini Advanced 我们对 Gemini Advanced 进行了三种类型的外部测试：• 优先用户计划（Priority User Program）：该计划收集了 120 名高级用户、关键影响者和思想领袖的反馈。该计划通过用户界面收集安全及其他领域实时反馈，并尽可能进行深度访谈。重点领域包括安全性和角色、功能、编码和指令能力，以及事实性。• 高级用户测试（Power Users Testing）：通过一个外部供应商招募的 50 名高级用户小组，对 Gemini Advanced 进行了多个领域的测试。• 安全测试（Security Testing）：通过合作伙伴机构招募的一组具有安全背景的外部测试人员，进行了安全性和提示注入测试、越狱以及用户界面安全故障测试。

paras.en: Following the completion of responsibility and safety reviews, internal model cards (Mitchell et al., 2019) for each approved version of the Gemini model are created for structured and consistent internal documentation of critical performance and responsibility metrics as well as to inform appropriate external communication of these metrics over time. We release external model and system cards on an ongoing basis within updates of our technical reports and in documentation for enterprise customers. See Appendix 10.1 for the Gemini Ultra model card. Additionally, online content covering terms of use, model distribution and access, and operational aspects such as change control, logging, monitoring and feedback can be found on relevant product websites, such as Gemini and Cloud Vertex AI. Some of the key aspects are linked to or described below: • Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy • Google Terms of service • Generative AI Terms of service • Google Cloud Platform Terms of service • Gemini Privacy Notice • Google Cloud Privacy Notice
paras.zh: 在完成责任与安全审查后，为每个批准的 Gemini 模型版本创建内部模型卡（Mitchell 等人，2019），用于关键性能和责任指标的结构化、一致性内部文档，并随时间推移告知这些指标的适当外部沟通。我们持续在技术报告更新和企业客户文档中发布外部模型和系统卡。请参见附录 10.1 了解 Gemini Ultra 模型卡。此外，涵盖使用条款、模型分发和访问以及操作方面（如变更控制、日志记录、监控和反馈）的在线内容可在相关产品网站上找到，例如 Gemini 和 Cloud Vertex AI。以下列出或链接了一些关键方面：• 生成式 AI 禁止使用政策 • Google 服务条款 • 生成式 AI 服务条款 • Google Cloud Platform 服务条款 • Gemini 隐私声明 • Google Cloud 隐私声明

paras.en: We have presented Gemini, a new family of models that advance multimodal model capabilities in text, code, image, audio, and video. Our most capable pre-trained model Gemini Ultra, alongside the post-trained Gemini Apps and Gemini API variants, make significant advances across the board. In the natural language domain, the performance gains from careful developments in data and model training at scale continue to deliver quality improvements, setting new state of the art in
paras.zh: 我们介绍了 Gemini，这是一个新的模型家族，在文本、代码、图像、音频和视频方面推进了多模态模型的能力。我们最强大的预训练模型 Gemini Ultra，以及后训练的 Gemini Apps 和 Gemini API 变体，在各个方面都取得了显著进展。在自然语言领域，通过精心开发数据和模型训练规模所带来的性能提升持续带来质量改进，在多个基准测试中设立了新的最优水平。

paras.en: several benchmarks. In particular, Gemini Ultra surpasses human-expert performance on the exam benchmark MMLU, scoring 90.0%, which has been a defacto measure of progress for LLMs ever since it was first released in 2020. In the multimodal domain, Gemini Ultra sets new state of the art on most of the image understanding, video understanding, and audio understanding benchmarks without task-specific modifications or tuning. In particular, Gemini Ultra's multimodal reasoning capabilities are evident from its state-of-the-art performance on the recent MMMU benchmark (Yue et al., 2023), that comprises questions about images requiring college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. Beyond the state-of-art results on benchmarks, what we are most excited about is the new use cases enabled by Gemini models. The new capabilities of Gemini models to parse complex images, such as charts or infographics, reason over interleaved sequences of images, audio, and text, and generate interleaved text and images as responses open a wide variety of new applications. As shown in figures throughout the report and appendix, Gemini models can enable new approaches in areas like education, everyday problem solving, multilingual communication, information summarization, extraction, and creativity. We expect that the users of these models will find all kinds of beneficial new uses that we have only scratched the surface of in our own investigations. Despite their impressive capabilities, we should note that there are limitations to the use of LLMs. There is a continued need for ongoing research and development on “hallucinations” generated by LLMs to ensure that model outputs are more reliable and verifiable. LLMs also struggle with tasks requiring high-level reasoning abilities like causal understanding, logical deduction, and counterfactual reasoning even though they achieve impressive performance on exam benchmarks. This underscores the need for more challenging and robust evaluations to measure their true understanding as the current state-of-the-art LLMs saturate many benchmarks. The Gemini family is a further step towards our mission to solve intelligence, advance science and benefit humanity, and we are enthusiastic to see how these models are used by our colleagues at Google and beyond. We build on many innovations in machine learning, data, infrastructure, and responsible development – areas that we have been pursuing at Google for over a decade. The models we present in this report provide a strong foundation towards our broader future goal to develop a large-scale, modularized system that will have broad generalization capabilities across many modalities.
paras.zh: 特别是在考试基准 MMLU 上，Gemini Ultra 超越了人类专家水平，得分 90.0%，自 2020 年首次发布以来，该基准一直是衡量大型语言模型（LLMs）进展的事实标准。在多模态领域，Gemini Ultra 在大多数图像理解、视频理解和音频理解基准上无需特定任务修改或调整就设立了新的最优水平。Gemini Ultra 的多模态推理能力从其最近在 MMMU 基准（Yue 等人，2023）上的最优表现可见一斑，该基准包含需要大学水平学科知识和深思熟虑推理的图像问题。除了基准测试中的最优结果，最让我们兴奋的是 Gemini 模型所支持的新用例。Gemini 模型解析复杂图像（如图表或信息图）、推理交错序列的图像、音频和文本，以及生成交错的文本和图像作为响应的新能力，开启了广泛的新应用。如报告和附录中的图表所示，Gemini 模型可以在教育、日常问题解决、多语言通信、信息摘要、提取和创造力等领域实现新方法。我们期待这些模型的用户将发现各种有益的新用途，而我们在自己的研究中仅触及了表面。尽管能力令人印象深刻，但我们应该注意到 LLMs 使用的局限性。需要持续研究和开发 LLMs 产生的“幻觉”，以确保模型输出更加可靠和可验证。LLMs 在需要高级推理能力的任务（如因果理解、逻辑演绎和反事实推理）上仍然挣扎，尽管它们在考试基准上取得了令人印象深刻的表现。这强调了需要更具挑战性和稳健的评估来衡量其真实理解，因为当前最先进的 LLMs 已经饱和了许多基准测试。Gemini 家族是朝着我们解决智能、推进科学和造福人类的使命迈出的又一步，我们热切期待看到这些模型如何被 Google 及之外的同事使用。我们建立在机器学习、数据、基础设施和负责任开发方面的许多创新之上——这些是 Google 十多年来一直追求的领域。本报告中介绍的模型为我们更广泛的未来目标（开发一个大规模、模块化系统，具有跨多种模态的广泛泛化能力）提供了坚实的基础。

paras.en: The roles are defined as below: • Lead: Individual(s) responsible for the sub-team throughout the project. • Core Contributor: Individual that had significant impact throughout the project. • Contributor: Individual that had contributions to the project and was partially involved with the effort. • Program Lead: Responsible for the organizational aspects of the Gemini effort. • Overall Post-Training Lead: Responsible for the technical direction of post-training. • Overall Technical Lead: Responsible for the technical direction of the overall Gemini effort. Within each role, contributions are equal, and are listed in a randomized order. Ordering within each role does not indicate ordering of the contributions. Gemini is a cross-Google effort, with members from Google DeepMind (GDM), Google Research (GR), Bard/Assistant, Knowledge and Information (K&I), Core ML, Cloud, Labs, and more. We thank Aakanksha Chowdhery, Dustin Tran, Heng-Tze Cheng, Jack W. Rae, Kate Olszewska, Mariko Iinuma, Peter Humphreys, Shashi Narayan, and Steven Zheng for leading the preparation of this report. We also thank our reviewers and colleagues for their valuable discussions and feedback on the report — Alexandra Belias, Ana Ramalho, Anand Rao, Arielle Bier, Danielle Landress, Eleanor Tomlinson, Emily Hossellman, Gaby Pearl, Helen King, Hollie Dobson, Jaclyn Konzelmann, Jennifer
paras.zh: 角色定义如下：• 负责人：在整个项目中负责子团队的个人。• 核心贡献者：在整个项目中具有重大影响的个人。• 贡献者：对项目有贡献并部分参与工作的个人。• 项目负责人：负责 Gemini 项目组织方面的事务。• 后训练总体负责人：负责后训练的技术方向。• 总体技术负责人：负责整个 Gemini 项目的技术方向。在每个角色内，贡献均等，并按随机顺序列出。每个角色内的顺序并不表示贡献的排序。Gemini 是一个跨 Google 的合作项目，成员来自 Google DeepMind (GDM)、Google Research (GR)、Bard/Assistant、知识与信息 (K&I)、Core ML、Cloud、Labs 等部门。我们感谢 Aakanksha Chowdhery、Dustin Tran、Heng-Tze Cheng、Jack W. Rae、Kate Olszewska、Mariko Iinuma、Peter Humphreys、Shashi Narayan 和 Steven Zheng 领导本报告的编写。我们也感谢审稿人和同事们的宝贵讨论和对报告的反馈——Alexandra Belias、Ana Ramalho、Anand Rao、Arielle Bier、Danielle Landress、Eleanor Tomlinson、Emily Hossellman、Gaby Pearl、Helen King、Hollie Dobson、Jaclyn Konzelmann、Jennifer

paras.en: Gemini V1.0 is a new family of state-of-the-art language models, containing variants known as Nano, Pro and Ultra (ordered by parameter count) based on a decoder-only Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017a). Models are trained to support 32K context length, employing efficient attention mechanisms such as multi-query attention (Shazeer, 2019b). Gemini is trained jointly across image, audio, video and text data for the purpose of building a model with both strong generalist capabilities across modalities alongside cutting-edge understanding and reasoning performance in each respective domain. The post-trained models described in this model card are Gemini API and Gemini Apps model variants (Section 6) built on top of the Gemini Ultra pre-trained model. During the post-training process, additional architectural modifications are also made to support the training of multi-objective reward models for RLHF.
paras.zh: Gemini V1.0 是一个新的最先进语言模型系列，包含基于仅解码器 Transformer 架构（Vaswani 等人，2017a）的 Nano、Pro 和 Ultra（按参数数量排序）变体。模型训练支持 32K 上下文长度，采用高效的注意力机制，如多查询注意力（Shazeer，2019b）。Gemini 联合在图像、音频、视频和文本数据上进行训练，旨在构建一个既具备跨模态强大通用能力，又在各自领域拥有前沿理解和推理性能的模型。本模型卡中描述的后训练模型是基于 Gemini Ultra 预训练模型构建的 Gemini API 和 Gemini 应用模型变体（第 6 节）。在后训练过程中，还进行了额外的架构修改，以支持用于基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）的多目标奖励模型的训练。

paras.en: Text (e.g. a question, a prompt, a document(s) to be summarized), images, video, audio files.
paras.zh: 文本（例如问题、提示、待总结的文档）、图像、视频、音频文件。

paras.en: Generated text in response to the input (e.g. an answer to the question, a summary of multiple documents, comparing documents/videos). Usage
paras.zh: 针对输入生成的文本（例如问题的答案、多个文档的摘要、文档/视频比较）。用途

paras.en: Gemini is designed for accelerating research on language models, for use as a building block in features within Google products, and as a building block for select applications such as Gemini App and Search Generative Experience. Services and products built on top of Gemini Ultra are also being made available to external developers via Google Cloud Vertex API and Google Labs, with additional process and technical safeguards related to safety policies.
paras.zh: Gemini 旨在加速语言模型研究，作为 Google 产品中功能的构建块，以及作为 Gemini 应用和搜索生成体验等特定应用的构建块。基于 Gemini Ultra 构建的服务和产品也通过 Google Cloud Vertex API 和 Google Labs 提供给外部开发者，并附有与安全策略相关的额外流程和技术保障。

paras.en: Gemini should not be made available as part of a general-purpose service or product, or used within a specific downstream application without a prior assessment and mitigation of the safety and fairness concerns specific to the downstream use.
paras.zh: Gemini 不应作为通用服务或产品的一部分提供，也不应在未事先评估和缓解下游使用特有的安全与公平问题的情况下用于特定的下游应用。

paras.en: Hardware: Training was conducted on TPUv4 and TPUv5e (Jouppi et al., 2020, 2023). Software: JAX (Bradbury et al., 2018), ML Pathways (Dean, 2021). JAX allows researchers to leverage the latest generation of hardware, including TPUs, for faster and more efficient training of large models. ML Pathways is infrastructure software to support Google's efforts to build artificially intelligent systems capable of generalizing across multiple tasks. This is especially suitable for foundation models, including large language models like the Gemini V1.0 models. Together, JAX and ML Pathways are used as described in Section 3. The 'single controller' programming model of JAX and ML Pathways allows a single Python process to orchestrate the entire training run, dramatically simplifying the development workflow.
paras.zh: 硬件：训练在 TPUv4 和 TPUv5e 上进行（Jouppi 等, 2020, 2023）。软件：JAX（Bradbury 等, 2018）、ML Pathways（Dean, 2021）。JAX 使研究人员能够利用最新一代硬件（包括 TPU），实现更快、更高效的大模型训练。ML Pathways 是一种基础设施软件，支持谷歌构建能够跨多个任务泛化的人工智能系统。这对于基础模型（包括像 Gemini V1.0 这样的大语言模型）特别适用。JAX 和 ML Pathways 一起使用，如第 3 节所述。JAX 和 ML Pathways 的“单控制器”编程模型允许单个 Python 进程协调整个训练运行，极大地简化了开发工作流程。

paras.en: Initial pretraining used random initialization. Post-training was initialized from checkpoints obtained at the later stages of pretraining. These checkpoints were fine-tuned using supervised fine-tuning, and subsequently used to initialize reward model training and RLHF.
paras.zh: 初始预训练使用随机初始化。后训练从预训练后期获得的检查点开始初始化。这些检查点通过有监督微调进行微调，随后用于初始化奖励模型训练和基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）。

paras.en: Gemini models are trained on a dataset that is both multimodal and multilingual. Our pre-training dataset uses data from web documents, books, and code, and includes image, audio, and video data. Refer to Section 4 (Pre-Training Dataset) for further details.
paras.zh: Gemini 模型在一个既多模态又多语言的数据集上进行训练。我们的预训练数据集使用来自网络文档、书籍和代码的数据，并包括图像、音频和视频数据。更多细节请参见第 4 节（预训练数据集）。

paras.en: We compare pre- and post-trained Gemini Ultra models to a suite of external LLMs and our previous best model PaLM 2 across a series of text-based academic benchmarks covering reasoning, reading comprehension, STEM, and coding. We also evaluate Gemini models on four different multimodal capabilities: high-level object recognition using captioning or question-answering tasks such as VQAv2; fine-grained transcription using tasks such as TextVQA and DocVQA requiring the model to recognize low-level details; chart understanding requiring spatial understanding of input layout using ChartQA and InfographicVQA tasks; and multimodal reasoning using tasks such as Ai2D, MathVista and MMMU. Refer to Section 5 (Evaluation) for further details.
paras.zh: 我们将预训练和后训练的 Gemini Ultra 模型与一系列外部大语言模型以及我们之前的最佳模型 PaLM 2 在一系列基于文本的学术基准上进行比较，涵盖推理、阅读理解、STEM 和编码。我们还评估了 Gemini 模型的四种不同多模态能力：通过字幕或问答任务（如 VQAv2）进行的高级物体识别；通过需要模型识别低层细节的任务（如 TextVQA 和 DocVQA）进行的细粒度转录；通过 ChartQA 和 InfographicVQA 任务进行的需要空间理解输入布局的图表理解；以及通过 Ai2D、MathVista 和 MMMU 等任务进行的多模态推理。更多细节请参见第 5 节（评估）。

paras.en: For post-training, we first collect a diverse set of prompts that are representative of real-world use cases. We then collect demonstration data of what the model's output should be for a given prompt for supervised fine-tuning. We further collect different possible responses to a given prompt, and collect feedback data over these to train reward models. Refer to Section 6.3 (Post-Training Methods and Data) for further details. Evaluation Results
paras.zh: 对于后训练，我们首先收集一组多样化的提示，这些提示代表真实世界的使用场景。然后，我们收集对于给定提示模型输出应该是什么的演示数据，用于有监督微调。我们进一步收集给定提示的不同可能响应，并收集关于这些响应的反馈数据来训练奖励模型。更多细节请参见第 6.3 节（后训练方法与数据）。评估结果

paras.en: See Section 5 (Evaluation) and Section 6.4 (Post-Training Human Evaluation). Model Usage & Limitations
paras.zh: 参见第 5 节（评估）和第 6.4 节（后训练人工评估）。模型使用与限制

paras.en: For an analysis of risks and sensitive uses associated with the Gemini models, see Section 7.1 (Impact Assessment).
paras.zh: 有关 Gemini 模型相关风险和敏感用途的分析，请参见第 7.1 节（影响评估）。

paras.en: Gemini models can exhibit limitations outlined in Section 7.1 (Impact Assessment). Gemini models should not be used for downstream applications without further analysis of potential harm in the proposed downstream application.
paras.zh: Gemini 模型可能存在第 7.1 节（影响评估）中概述的局限性。在没有对拟定的下游应用进行进一步潜在危害分析的情况下，不应将 Gemini 模型用于下游应用。

paras.en: A reflection on the potential risks and impacts of the Gemini V1.0 models can be found in Section 7 (Responsible Deployment). For evaluation details for a range of risks, see Section 7.4 (Safety Evaluations).
paras.zh: 关于 Gemini V1.0 模型潜在风险和影响的反思可在第 7 节（负责任部署）中找到。有关一系列风险的评估详情，请参见第 7.4 节（安全评估）。

full.secZh: 10.2 MMLU 基准上的思维链比较

paras.en: We contrast several chain-of-thought approaches on MMLU and discuss their results in this section. We proposed a new approach where the model produces k chain-of-thought samples, selects the majority vote if the model is confident above a threshold, and otherwise defers to the greedy sample choice. The 73
paras.zh: 我们在 MMLU 上对比了几种思维链方法，并讨论了它们的结果。我们提出了一种新方法：模型生成 k 个思维链样本，若模型置信度高于阈值则选择多数投票，否则退回到贪心样本选择。这 73

paras.en: thresholds are optimized for each model based on their validation split performance. The proposed approach is referred to as uncertainty-routed chain-of-thought. The intuition behind this approach is that chain-of-thought samples might degrade performance compared to the maximum-likelihood decision when the model is demonstrably inconsistent. We compare the gains from the proposed approach on both Gemini Ultra and GPT-4 in Figure 9. We find that Gemini Ultra benefits more from this approach compared to using only chain-of-thought samples. GPT-4’s performance improves from 84.2% with greedy sampling to 87.3% with uncertainty-routed chain-of-thought approach with 32 samples, but it already achieves these gains from using 32 chain-of-thought samples. In contrast, Gemini Ultra improves its performance significantly from 84.0% with greedy sampling to 90.0% with uncertainty-routed chain-of-thought approach with 32 samples while it marginally improves to 85.0% with the use of 32 chain-of-thought samples only. GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613)
paras.zh: 个阈值根据每个模型在验证集上的表现进行优化。所提出的方法称为不确定性路由思维链。该方法背后的直觉是，当模型明显不一致时，思维链样本可能会降低性能，相比最大似然决策更差。我们在图 9 中对比了所提出的方法在 Gemini Ultra 和 GPT-4 上的增益。我们发现，Gemini Ultra 从该方法中获益更多，相比于仅使用思维链样本。GPT-4 的性能从贪心采样的 84.2%提升到使用 32 个样本的不确定性路由思维链的 87.3%，但它仅使用 32 个思维链样本就已经达到这一增益。相比之下，Gemini Ultra 的性能从贪心采样的 84.0%显著提升到使用 32 个样本的不确定性路由思维链的 90.0%，而仅使用 32 个思维链样本时仅提升到 85.0%。GPT-4（gpt-4-0613）

paras.en: We use more than 50 benchmarks as a holistic harness to evaluate the Gemini models across text, image, audio and video. We provide a detailed list of benchmarking tasks for six different capabilities in text understanding and generation: factuality, long context, math/science, reasoning, summarization, and multilinguality. We also enumerate the benchmarks used for image understanding, video understanding, and audio understanding tasks. • Factuality: We use 5 benchmarks: BoolQ (Clark et al., 2019), NaturalQuestions-Closed (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019a), NaturalQuestions-Retrieved (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019a), RealtimeQA (Kasai et al., 2022b), TydiQA-noContext and TydiQA-goldP (Clark et al., 2020). • Long Context: We use 6 benchmarks: NarrativeQA (Kočiský et al., 2018), Scrolls-Qasper, Scrolls-Quality (Shaham et al., 2022), XLsum (En), XLSum (non-English languages) (Hasan et al., 2021), and one other internal benchmark. • Math/Science: We use 8 benchmarks: GSM8k (with CoT) (Cobbe et al., 2021), Hendryck’s MATH pass@1 (Hendrycks et al., 2021b), MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a), Math-StackExchange, Math-AMC 2022-2023 problems, and three other internal benchmarks. • Reasoning: We use 7 benchmarks: BigBench Hard (with CoT) (Srivastava et al., 2022; Suzgun et al., 2022), CLRS (Veličković et al., 2022), Proof Writer (Tafjord et al., 2020), Reasoning-Fermi problems (Kalyan et al., 2021), Lambada (Paperno et al., 2016), HellaSwag (Zellers et al., 2019), DROP (Dua et al., 2019). • Summarization: We use 5 benchmarks: XL Sum (English), XL Sum (non-English languages) (Hasan et al., 2021), WikiLingua (non-English languages), WikiLingua (English) (Ladhak et al., 2020), XSum (Narayan et al., 2018). • Multilinguality: We use 10 benchmarks: XLSum (Non-English languages) (Hasan et al., 2021), WMT22 (Kocmi et al., 2022), WMT23 (Tom et al., 2023), FRMT (Riley et al., 2023), WikiLingua (Non-English languages) (Ladhak et al., 2020), TydiQA (no context), TydiQA (GoldP) (Clark et al., 2020), MGSM (Shi et al., 2023), translated MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a), NTREX (Federmann et al., 2022), FLORES-200 (Team et al., 2022). • Image and Video: We use 9 benchmarks for image understanding: MMMU (Yue et al., 2023), TextVQA (Singh et al., 2019), DocVQA (Mathew et al., 2021), ChartQA (Masry et al., 2022), InfographicVQA (Mathew et al., 2022), MathVista (Lu et al., 2023), AI2D (Kembhavi et al., 2016), VQAv2 (Goyal et al., 2017), XM3600 (Thapliyal et al., 2022) for multi-lingual image understanding, and 6 benchmarks for video understanding: VATEX (Wang et al., 2019) for captioning in two different languages, YouCook2 (Zhou et al., 2018), NextQA (Xiao et al., 2021), ActivityNet-QA (Yu et al., 2019), and Perception Test MCQA (Pătrăucean et al., 2023). • Audio: We use 5 benchmarks including automatic speech recognition (ASR) tasks such as FLEURS (Conneau et al., 2023), VoxPopuli (Wang et al., 2021), Multi-lingual Librispeech (Pratap et al., 2020), and automatic speech translation task such as CoVoST 2 (Wang et al., 2020).
paras.zh:
我们使用超过 50 个基准测试作为整体框架，评估 Gemini 模型在文本、图像、音频和视频上的表现。我们提供了文本理解与生成六个不同能力的基准测试任务详细列表：事实性、长上下文、数学/科学、推理、摘要生成和多语言性。我们还列举了用于图像理解、视频理解和音频理解任务的基准测试。
- **事实性**：我们使用 5 个基准：BoolQ (Clark et al., 2019)、NaturalQuestions-Closed (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019a)、NaturalQuestions-Retrieved (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019a)、RealtimeQA (Kasai et al., 2022b)、TydiQA-noContext 和 TydiQA-goldP (Clark et al., 2020)。
- **长上下文**：我们使用 6 个基准：NarrativeQA (Kočiský et al., 2018)、Scrolls-Qasper、Scrolls-Quality (Shaham et al., 2022)、XLsum（英文）、XLSum（非英语语言）(Hasan et al., 2021)，以及另一个内部基准。
- **数学/科学**：我们使用 8 个基准：GSM8k（含思维链）(Cobbe et al., 2021)、Hendryck 的 MATH pass@1 (Hendrycks et al., 2021b)、MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a)、Math-StackExchange、Math-AMC 2022-2023 问题，以及三个内部基准。
- **推理**：我们使用 7 个基准：BigBench Hard（含思维链）(Srivastava et al., 2022; Suzgun et al., 2022)、CLRS (Veličković et al., 2022)、Proof Writer (Tafjord et al., 2020)、Reasoning-Fermi problems (Kalyan et al., 2021)、Lambada (Paperno et al., 2016)、HellaSwag (Zellers et al., 2019)、DROP (Dua et al., 2019)。
- **摘要生成**：我们使用 5 个基准：XL Sum（英文）、XL Sum（非英语语言）(Hasan et al., 2021)、WikiLingua（非英语语言）、WikiLingua（英文）(Ladhak et al., 2020)、XSum (Narayan et al., 2018)。
- **多语言性**：我们使用 10 个基准：XLSum（非英语语言）(Hasan et al., 2021)、WMT22 (Kocmi et al., 2022)、WMT23 (Tom et al., 2023)、FRMT (Riley et al., 2023)、WikiLingua（非英语语言）(Ladhak et al., 2020)、TydiQA（无上下文）、TydiQA（GoldP）(Clark et al., 2020)、MGSM (Shi et al., 2023)、翻译后的 MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a)、NTREX (Federmann et al., 2022)、FLORES-200 (Team et al., 2022)。
- **图像与视频**：对于图像理解，我们使用 9 个基准：MMMU (Yue et al., 2023)、TextVQA (Singh et al., 2019)、DocVQA (Mathew et al., 2021)、ChartQA (Masry et al., 2022)、InfographicVQA (Mathew et al., 2022)、MathVista (Lu et al., 2023)、AI2D (Kembhavi et al., 2016)、VQAv2 (Goyal et al., 2017)、XM3600 (Thapliyal et al., 2022) 用于多语言图像理解；对于视频理解，使用 6 个基准：VATEX (Wang et al., 2019) 用于两种语言的字幕生成、YouCook2 (Zhou et al., 2018)、NextQA (Xiao et al., 2021)、ActivityNet-QA (Yu et al., 2019) 以及 Perception Test MCQA (Pătrăucean et al., 2023)。
- **音频**：我们使用 5 个基准，包括自动语音识别（ASR）任务如 FLEURS (Conneau et al., 2023)、VoxPopuli (Wang et al., 2021)、多语言 Librispeech (Pratap et al., 2020)，以及自动语音翻译任务如 CoVoST 2 (Wang et al., 2020)。

paras.en: This section shows sample qualitative examples from prompting the Gemini Ultra model. Some illustrative examples of multimodal reasoning for image understanding tasks over charts, natural images and memes are shown in Figures 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, and 17. Figure 12 shows an example of image generation capabilities of Gemini Ultra where the user generates an interleaved sequence of image and text to design a blog post. Beyond English, Figure 18 shows the model's capability to understand images in a multilingual setting. Gemini models also show strong performance on multimodal image understanding and reasoning in mathematics, as shown in Figures 14, 20 and 21. Figure 22 is an example of complex multimodal reasoning demonstrating how the model composes complex image understanding, code generation, and instruction following capabilities for a given user task. In Figure 19, we see another example of the model being able to generate working code and follow complex user instructions. Finally, Figure 23 shows an example of Gemini Ultra's capability of understanding video by reasoning over temporally connected set of frames.
paras.zh: 本节展示了对 Gemini Ultra 模型进行提示（prompting）后的示例定性结果。图 10、11、13、15、16 和 17 展示了一些针对图表、自然图像和表情包等图像理解任务的多模态推理示例。图 12 展示了 Gemini Ultra 的图像生成能力，用户生成交错的图像和文本序列来设计一篇博客文章。除了英语，图 18 展示了模型在多语言环境下理解图像的能力。Gemini 模型在数学领域的多模态图像理解和推理中同样表现出色，如图 14、20 和 21 所示。图 22 是一个复杂多模态推理的示例，展示了模型如何综合运用复杂的图像理解、代码生成和指令遵循能力来完成给定的用户任务。在图 19 中，我们看到了模型能够生成可用代码并遵循复杂用户指令的另一个示例。最后，图 23 展示了 Gemini Ultra 通过对时间上连续的帧序列进行推理来理解视频的能力。
